name: WV-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+20 district partisan lean in deep-red West Virginia
Incumbent Riley Moore with a large fundraising edge ($1.56M vs $250K)
No polling and no expert ratings; markets price a Republican win at ~96%
Challenger Ace Parsi is underfunded with minimal cash on hand
model.rationale: The R+20 lean, Moore's incumbency and dominant fundraising advantage, and Polymarket pricing the Democrat at just 3% all point to a safe Republican hold. No polls or expert ratings provide any basis to move off the fundamentals.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or a major Moore scandal could narrow the race, though nothing in the evidence suggests that is likely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
West Virginia's second district is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly R+20. First-term incumbent Riley Moore is running for reelection and holds an overwhelming financial advantage, having raised about $1.56 million with $818,000 on hand, while Democrat Ace Parsi has raised about $250,000 with $115,000 available. No outside groups are actively opposing Moore.

There are no public general-election polls and no expert raters have flagged the race as competitive. Prediction markets give Moore roughly a 96% chance of winning. With the fundamentals, money, and market pricing all aligned, the district remains safely in Republican hands.
